payload.reason: The evidence indicates that categories exist across languages and cultures, suggesting that languages share categories based on common cognitive structures and properties.

claims.text: Categories such as animal or furniture are fundamental cognitive building blocks that exist across cultures, allowing efficient representation of the world.
The study shows that meaningful categories emerge across languages, indicating that categorization is influenced by language but also shares commonalities.
The Bayesian model used in the study learns meaningful categories from natural language text across multiple languages, demonstrating shared categorical structures.
